answer:
Yes. MDX compiles to the @sleekstack/ui JSX runtime with no changes to ui. All 27 hand-written pages and the 13 generated api pages compile and render through `renderToString`. Two MDX options and one small rehype pass are needed to work around ui's string-only attributes. **Setup.** Throwaway probe at the session scratchpad `mdx-probe/` (outside the repo, no repo files or lockfiles touched). @sleekstack/ui is the workspace `packages/ui` dist at branch chart-docs-rebuild (4780eb0), symlinked in. Versions: Node 22.20.0, @mdx-js/mdx 3.1.1 (the version fumadocs-mdx 12.0.3 resolves in the repo), remark-gfm 4.0.1, remark-frontmatter 5.0.0, remark-mdx-frontmatter 6.0.0, rehype-slug 6.0.0, shiki and @shikijs/rehype 4.5.0, @shikijs/transformers 4.5.0, effect 3.21.2 (ui's copy), tsx 4.23.15. Each page went through `compile(src, { jsxImportSource: '@sleekstack/ui', ... })`, then the ESM was written out and imported, and `renderToString(MDXContent({ components }), { layer: Layer.empty })` rendered it. A second check used `evaluate(src, { ...uiJsxRuntime })`. **What works** - The MDX output calls `jsx`, `jsxs` and `Fragment` from `@sleekstack/ui/jsx-runtime`. `MDXContent(props)` returns an `Effect`, which drops straight into a ui tree and into `renderToString`. - Headings, paragraphs, lists, inline code, emphasis and links work, and so do GFM tables once remark-gfm is added (index.mdx: 1 table, 22 cells; benchmarks.mdx: 4 tables, 338 cells). - The components map works. An `a` override rewrote 14 internal links on ui.mdx. A custom `` component (callout-shaped) and a `wrapper` layout both render, because ui runs map entries as component instances. - Text in code is escaped (`<Node`). - Timing: compile takes about 5-90 ms per page and about 320 ms for the first shiki page, which is highlighter init. Render takes 2-18 ms. **What breaks, and the fix for each** 1. **Frontmatter.** Without remark-frontmatter, the YAML block renders as an `
` plus a setext `

`. Fix: remark-frontmatter + remark-mdx-frontmatter. This exports `frontmatter` (title, description) for nav and ``. 2. **Code blocks.** The pages have no fences. All code comes from fumadocs `path` (53 uses across the pages). Without a plugin it renders as a literal `` element. Fix: a remark plugin of about 20 lines that reads the file and replaces the include with a `code` node, taking the language from the file extension. The probe's stand-in reproduced all 9 code blocks on ui.mdx. Snippet tests are unaffected because they read the same files. 3. **Style attributes.** MDX turns a hast `style` string into a JSX object, and ui's `split` stringifies every attribute, so it renders as `style="[object Object]"`. This came from two places: - shiki token colours (945 spans on ui.mdx). Fix: a rehype pass after shiki that hoists every `style` into a hashed class and emits one CSS file. The probe's version is about 15 lines. Stock `transformerStyleToClass` only caught the `pre`, because with a single theme the token colour is not in `htmlStyle`. - GFM column alignment. Fix: the MDX option `tableCellAlignToStyle: false`, which emits `align="right"`. The alternative is for ui to serialize object `style` values, which would be a ui change. 4. **Heading ids.** Headings have no ids, so there are no anchors and no TOC. Fix: rehype-slug (ids on 7 headings for ui.mdx, verified). A TOC export, like fumadocs' remark-heading, is not probed. It would be a small remark plugin. 5. **Attribute case.** By default MDX emits `className` and `tabIndex`. ui renames `className`, but `tabIndex` passes through as-is. Fix: `elementAttributeNameCase: 'html'`, which gives `class` and `tabindex`. 6. **ui serializer bug (not MDX).** `renderToString` has no void-element list, so it writes `

`, `
` and ``. Browsers read `
` as a second `
`, which doubles the break on markdown hard breaks. A stray `` or `` is just ignored. The generated api pages carry `
` on every page (up to 33). This should be fixed in ui's string serializer (`packages/ui/src/string.ts`) as part of the rebuild. 7. **Loading ui's dist under plain Node ESM fails.** The dist uses extensionless relative imports (bundler resolution). The probe ran under tsx, and Vite or start's bundler would resolve them. A raw-node build script cannot import `@sleekstack/ui` as built today. 8. ui has no raw-HTML escape hatch, so pre-highlighted HTML strings cannot be injected. Highlighting has to stay in hast, before MDX turns it into JSX, which is how the shiki path above works. **Highlighting at build time.** Add `@shikijs/rehype` as a rehype plugin at compile time (theme plus langs ts and tsx), then the style-to-class pass. The output is static `
` markup plus a generated CSS file, with no client JS. Dual light and dark themes would use shiki's `themes` and `defaultColor: false` (CSS variables), still hoisted to classes. Not probed.

**Smallest viable renderer.** Build or SSR step, per content file:

`compile(src, { jsxImportSource: '@sleekstack/ui', elementAttributeNameCase: 'html', tableCellAlignToStyle: false, remarkPlugins: [remarkFrontmatter, remarkMdxFrontmatter, remarkGfm, include], rehypePlugins: [rehypeSlug, [rehypeShiki, opts], styleToClass] })`

This gives an ESM module exporting `default` (MDXContent) and `frontmatter`. A docs layout component then renders `{MDXContent({ components: { a: DocLink } })}`, and `renderToString(page, { layer })` turns the result into HTML. This needs no fumadocs, React or Next. `evaluate()` with the ui runtime spread in also works, for an on-the-fly server path. The remaining pieces to build are the include plugin, the style-to-class pass, a TOC/heading export, nav from `meta.json`, and the ui void-element fix.

Evidence: scratchpad `mdx-probe/probe.mjs` (stages bare, full and fixed), `mdx-probe/void.mjs`, and the compiled `.mjs`, `.html` and `shiki.css` under `mdx-probe/out/` (session-scoped, throwaway).
